matthew.21.p1.b1.text: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two disciples,

matthew.21.p1.b2.text: Go into the village ahead of you, and at once you will find a donkey tied there, with her colt beside her.

matthew.21.p1.b3.text: Untie them and bring them to Me.

matthew.21.p1.b4.text: If anyone questions you, tell him that the Lord needs them, and he will send them right away.

matthew.21.p2.b1.text: This took place to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet … Say to the Daughter of Zion

matthew.21.p2.b2.text: See, your King comes to you, gentle and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.

matthew.21.p2.b3.text: So the disciples went and did as Jesus had directed them. They brought the donkey and the colt and laid their cloaks on them, and Jesus sat on them.

matthew.21.p3.b1.text: A massive crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.

matthew.21.p3.b2.text: Hosanna to the Son of David!

matthew.21.p3.b3.text: Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!

matthew.21.p4.b1.text: When Jesus had entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred and asked

matthew.21.p4.b3.text: This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.

matthew.21.p5.b1.text: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and drove out all who were buying and selling there.

matthew.21.p5.b2.text: He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.

matthew.21.p5.b3.text: It is written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer.’

matthew.21.p5.b4.text: But you are making it ‘a den of robbers.’

matthew.21.p6.b1.text: The blind and the lame came to Him at the temple

matthew.21.p7.b1.text: But the chief priests and scribes were indignant when they saw the wonders He performed and the children shouting in the temple courts

matthew.21.p7.b2.text: Hosanna to the Son of David!

matthew.21.p7.b3.text: Do you hear what these children are saying?

matthew.21.p7.b4.text: Yes … Have you never read: ‘From the mouths of children and infants You have ordained praise’?

matthew.21.p8.b1.text: Then He left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where He spent the night.

matthew.21.p8.b2.text: In the morning, as Jesus was returning to the city, He was hungry.

matthew.21.p8.b3.text: May you never bear fruit again!

matthew.21.p9.b1.text: How did the fig tree wither so quickly?

matthew.21.p9.b2.text: Truly I tell you … if you have faith and do not doubt

matthew.21.p9.b3.text: but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ it will happen.

matthew.21.p9.b4.text: If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer.”

matthew.21.p10.b1.text: When Jesus returned to the temple courts and began to teach, the chief priests and elders of the people came up to Him.

matthew.21.p10.b2.text: By what authority are You doing these things?

matthew.21.p10.b3.text: And who gave You this authority?

matthew.21.p10.b4.text: I will also ask you one question … and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

matthew.21.p11.b1.text: What was the source of John’s baptism? Was it from heaven or from men?

matthew.21.p11.b2.text: If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’

matthew.21.p11.b3.text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ we are afraid of the people, for they all regard John as a prophet.”

matthew.21.p11.b5.text: Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

matthew.21.p12.b1.text: Son, go and work today in the vineyard.

matthew.21.p12.b4.text: But later he changed his mind and went.

matthew.21.p13.b1.text: Which of the two did the will of his father?

matthew.21.p13.b3.text: Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and prostitutes are entering the kingdom of God before you.

matthew.21.p13.b4.text: but the tax collectors and prostitutes did. And even after you saw this, you did not repent and believe him.

matthew.21.p14.b2.text: There was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower.

matthew.21.p14.b3.text: Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.

matthew.21.p14.b4.text: When the harvest time drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit.

matthew.21.p15.b1.text: But the tenants seized his servants. They beat one, killed another, and stoned a third.

matthew.21.p15.b2.text: Again, he sent other servants, more than the first group. But the tenants did the same to them.

matthew.21.p16.b1.text: This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.

matthew.21.p16.b2.text: So they seized him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.

matthew.21.p16.b3.text: Therefore, when the owner of the vineyard returns, what will he do to those tenants?”

matthew.21.p16.b4.text: He will bring those wretches to a wretched end … and will rent out the vineyard to other tenants who will give him his share of the fruit at harvest time.

matthew.21.p17.b1.text: Have you never read in the Scriptures

matthew.21.p17.b2.text: The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes

matthew.21.p17.b3.text: Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit.

matthew.21.p17.b4.text: Although they wanted to arrest Him, they were afraid of the crowds, because the people regarded Him as a prophet.
